stem: A 55-year-old man becomes constipated 2 weeks after starting an over-the-counter cough syrup. The label lists acetaminophen, dextromethorphan, guaifenesin, loratadine and phenylephrine.
oneliner: 55M + constipation 2 wk after starting OTC cough syrup (acetaminophen, dextromethorphan, guaifenesin, loratadine, phenylephrine) → which ingredient?
ask: Which ingredient most likely caused his constipation?

whyNot.A: Danger is **liver injury** in overdose, not constipation

why: **Dextromethorphan** is an **opioid-related cough suppressant**, and opioid-like drugs slow the gut and cause constipation.

drug.name: Dextromethorphan
drug.how: Acts centrally to suppress the cough reflex
drug.watch: Constipation, sedation; serotonin syndrome with SSRIs or MAOIs; abused at high doses

stem: A 29-year-old woman with idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension starts an oral endothelin receptor antagonist. Her baseline blood tests are normal, and she is told she must come in every month for blood work and a pregnancy test. She asks what the blood tests are watching for.
oneliner: 29F + idiopathic pulmonary arterial hypertension + new oral endothelin receptor antagonist + monthly blood tests and pregnancy tests → what is monitored?
ask: Which of the following adverse effects is being monitored?

whyNot.B: **Nitroprusside** toxicity during a prolonged infusion; her drug is **oral**
whyNot.C: **PDE-5 inhibitor** (sildenafil) effect; her drug is an **endothelin receptor antagonist**
whyNot.D: **ACE inhibitor** effect, and cough is not followed by **blood work**
whyNot.E: **ACE inhibitor, ARB or spironolactone** effect; her drug does not act on the **renin-angiotensin-aldosterone** system

why: An **oral endothelin receptor antagonist** for pulmonary arterial hypertension is **bosentan**. It is **hepatotoxic** (**monthly liver enzymes**) and **teratogenic** (**monthly pregnancy test**), so it is given only through a restricted program.

drug.name: Bosentan
drug.how: Blocks ET-A and ET-B receptors, reducing pulmonary vasoconstriction
drug.watch: Hepatotoxicity (monthly liver tests), teratogenicity (monthly pregnancy test), anemia, edema; induces CYP3A4 and lowers hormonal contraceptive levels

idea.rule: Endothelin receptor antagonists are teratogenic, and bosentan is also liver-toxic, so monitoring is monthly.
also: Ambrisentan and macitentan carry the same teratogenic warning
Riociguat, another PAH drug, also needs monthly pregnancy tests
Bosentan induces CYP3A4, so hormonal contraception alone is not reliable
